title: Evidence b(i)ased medicine—selective reporting from studies sponsored by pharmaceutical industry: review of studies in new drug applications
authors: Melander H, Ahlqvist-Rastad J, Meijer G, Beermann B
population: 42 placebo-controlled trials of five SSRIs in major depression submitted to the Swedish Medical Products Agency for marketing approval, compared with publications from 1983 to 1999; analysis by agency staff
funder: Funding: None. All authors were staff of the Swedish Medical Products Agency.
result: 21 trials contributed to at least two publications each and three to five publications; trials with significant drug effects were published as stand-alone papers more often than trials with non-significant results; many publications reported only the more favourable per-protocol analyses and ignored the intention-to-treat results. The authors concluded that recommending a specific SSRI from publicly available data alone is likely to rest on biased evidence.
